summary: Gangwon stands under the national framework of South Korea. The source inventory records no province-specific law, court ruling, enforcement action, incident, or institution for Gangwon. The two legal standards it documents, the restroom-access damages ruling and the removal of the surgical prerequisite for a registered sex change, are national in scope and are recorded as applying in the province with no Gangwon-specific case attached to either. A trans visitor to Gangwon therefore faces the national legal position with no documented province-level variation.
tangentialFactors: The standards that reach Gangwon were set by courts elsewhere in the country, in the capital and in other provinces, rather than by any Gangwon court; the inventory records no Gangwon bench ruling on restroom access or on registered-sex change. The province's position on these questions is derived from national litigation rather than from local adjudication, and no Gangwon authority is recorded as having contested, narrowed, or extended that position.
localsOnly: No Gangwon-specific measure appears in the inventory. No provincial ordinance, school policy, hospital protocol, or police guidance issued by Gangwon authorities on restroom access, registered-sex change, or the accommodation of transgender patients is documented. Residents of the province depend on the national framework for these questions, and the inventory records no provincial institution acting on them.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Gangwon-specific incident, enforcement action, or court ruling is documented; whether any exists is unresolved in the source inventory.

The national survey data in the inventory is not disaggregated by province, so no Gangwon-specific figure can be derived from it.

Whether Gangwon provincial or municipal authorities have issued any guidance on restroom access, gender-marker change, or hospital accommodation for transgender patients is not sourced.
